issues.description: HAS_PERCENTAGE regex omits the case-insensitive flag while HAS_KEYWORD has it, breaking symmetry and missing uppercase percentage selectors like FROM/TO -> 0% mapping
issues.detail: PERCENTAGE_SELECTORS includes literal '0%' and '100%' which are case-agnostic, but the surrounding selector tokens are matched without /i. More importantly, HAS_KEYWORD uses /i, so a selector like '50%' would not trip HAS_PERCENTAGE under primary='keyword' if any future keyword variant appears. State the invariant: the filter must be a strict superset of cases the walker would flag. Audit each branch against that invariant.

issues.description: HAS_NAMED/HAS_NUMERIC pre-filters fire on the full decl.value without isolating the font-weight position in the font shorthand, risking false negatives on edge values
issues.detail: For 'font' shorthand, the weight token is one of several. The \b boundaries plus alternation will match 'bold' or '700' anywhere in the value, which is fine for positive matches, but the regex was built from fontWeightNonNumericKeywords plus fontWeightRelativeKeywords only. If decl.value contains 'normal' (a valid weight keyword shared with font-style), the early-return logic still holds, but please state and verify the invariant: 'every value the full parser would flag also matches the prefilter.'

issues.description: import-notation prefilter uses /url\(/i but does not account for comments or strings containing the literal text 'url('
issues.detail: A param like '"url(fake)"' would falsely trigger the slow path for primary='string' (harmless, just no speedup) and falsely skip for primary='url' (correctness risk). The latter is the concern: under primary='url', a string param containing 'url(' inside quotes would be skipped though the rule would otherwise flag it. Worth a quick test case.

issues.description: Regexes constructed from Sets/Maps lack literal-escaping; today's keyword lists are safe but the construction is fragile
issues.detail: HAS_NAMED, HAS_NUMERIC, HAS_PERCENTAGE, HAS_KEYWORD all interpolate set/map contents directly into RegExp source. Current contents are alphanumeric/percent, so it works. If a future keyword contains a regex metacharacter, the pattern silently corrupts. A small escapeRegExp helper would make the invariant ('the regex matches exactly these literals') hold by construction.

issues.description: Performance claim is unmeasured in the PR description; the optimization is plausible but the 3% should be demonstrated
issues.detail: Knuth's rule: measure before optimizing. The diff is a reasonable hot-path bypass, but no benchmark numbers, profile output, or before/after timings appear. For a perf PR touching six rules, a small benchmark table would let reviewers verify this is in the critical 3% and not premature work elsewhere.

issues.description: media-feature-range-notation context regex /(?:min|max)-/i is broader than needed and may match outside feature names
issues.detail: The pattern matches 'min-' or 'max-' anywhere in atRule.params. Media query params containing these substrings inside calc() expressions, custom property names, or comments would defeat the fast path (correctness-safe but the invariant is loose). Tightening to a word boundary or feature-name context would make the filter precise; current form is fine but worth a comment stating it's an over-approximation by design.

review.summary: UNDER-AUDITED. The optimization strategy is sound and follows a Knuthian principle correctly: bypass the expensive parser when a cheap prefilter proves the slow path cannot produce a finding. However, the invariant 'prefilter accepts every value the walker would flag' is not stated anywhere and not uniformly enforced — HAS_PERCENTAGE/HAS_KEYWORD have asymmetric case sensitivity, the regexes are built from data without literal-escaping, and the import-notation url(/string filter is naive about quoted strings. The performance win is also unmeasured in the PR; for a six-file perf change, a small benchmark would establish this is the critical 3%. Recommend stating the invariant in a comment per rule, adding escapeRegExp, and including before/after timings.
